source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 281: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions (variant 281): treat the initialization hang as an unproven symptom. Use an authorized disposable allocation, a finite watchdog, redacted logs, and automatic cleanup; do not change production settings. Keep launcher, image, placement, world size, framework, backend, and library versions fixed during diagnosis, and label every fact measured, estimated, or unknown.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-membership/rendezvous mismatch or collective-order divergence leaves at least one rank waiting. Competing hypotheses are incorrect GPU visibility or device mapping, stale or unreachable rendezvous state, a wrong interface/route/MTU/firewall path, topology or peer-access problems, container/shared-memory limits, and CPU/RAM/file-descriptor exhaustion. The primary hypothesis is falsified only when every rank reports the same fresh attempt ID, expected world size, unique global/local rank, host, rendezvous endpoint, visible device UUID, selected interface, and identical collective sequence, and a checksum-verified minimal all-reduce completes on every rank within the stated timeout.

Measurements: capture per-rank launch and process-group arguments with credentials redacted; rendezvous/store reachability and timestamps; rank arrival/exit and last-progress times; backend/framework/CUDA/driver versions; GPU visibility, UUIDs, peer access and PCIe/NVLink topology; interface, address, route, DNS, MTU and firewall state; placement; container device/shared-memory access; CPU, memory, file-descriptor and ulimit status; and watchdog/termination events. Preserve raw evidence read-only and record commands, units, sampling interval, and uncertainty.

Controlled experiment: first run the same minimal all-reduce on one node, then a reduced world, then the full placement, with identical payload, ordering, environment, timeout, and repeated trials (for example 5 per condition). Randomize trial order where practical. Record success rate, completion latency in ms, timeout stage, per-rank skew, CUDA/NCCL errors, selected transport/interface, and cleanup outcome. Change one factor at a time in disposable runs: explicit interface, fresh rendezvous namespace, device mapping, or placement; never mask a failure by disabling safety checks. Compare observed traces against the hypothesis and reject it when the invariant passes but the failure persists, or when a competing factor changes outcome with other variables held constant.

Confounders and mitigations: scheduler placement, transient fabric faults, clock skew, warm caches, stale processes, retries, background load, version drift, and altered trial order can mimic causality; pin or record them, use fresh namespaces, synchronize clocks, and report failed/aborted trials separately. Set a bounded timeout, kill only owned child processes, verify no orphaned ranks, redact secrets and host-sensitive data, and obtain authorization before network or environment changes. Roll back temporary variables, interface overrides, debug settings, and files after each trial. Evidence is required before assigning a root cause; provisional conclusions should include confidence and the next discriminating measurement.
risks: rank/order diagnosis can be confounded by transient transport or scheduler faults
debug artifacts may expose topology or endpoint metadata
controlled trials can leave orphaned processes if watchdog cleanup fails
evidence_required: per-rank rendezvous and collective timestamps
fresh-namespace repeated all-reduce results across single-node, reduced-world, and full-world conditions
version, topology, interface, resource, and cleanup records

Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions (variant 294): treat the initialization hang as an unproven symptom. Use an authorized disposable allocation, a finite watchdog, redacted logs, and automatic cleanup; do not change production settings. Keep launcher, image, placement, world size, framework, backend, and library versions fixed during diagnosis, and label every fact measured, estimated, or unknown.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-membership/rendezvous mismatch or collective-order divergence leaves at least one rank waiting. Competing hypotheses are incorrect GPU visibility or device mapping, stale or unreachable rendezvous state, a wrong interface/route/MTU/firewall path, topology or peer-access problems, container/shared-memory limits, and CPU/RAM/file-descriptor exhaustion. The primary hypothesis is falsified only when every rank reports the same fresh attempt ID, expected world size, unique global/local rank, host, rendezvous endpoint, visible device UUID, selected interface, and identical collective sequence, and a checksum-verified minimal all-reduce completes on every rank within the stated timeout.

Measurements: capture per-rank launch and process-group arguments with credentials redacted; rendezvous/store reachability and timestamps; rank arrival/exit and last-progress times; backend/framework/CUDA/driver versions; GPU visibility, UUIDs, peer access and PCIe/NVLink topology; interface, address, route, DNS, MTU and firewall state; placement; container device/shared-memory access; CPU, memory, file-descriptor and ulimit status; and watchdog/termination events. Preserve raw evidence read-only and record commands, units, sampling interval, and uncertainty.

Controlled experiment: first run the same minimal all-reduce on one node, then a reduced world, then the full placement, with identical payload, ordering, environment, timeout, and repeated trials (for example 5 per condition). Randomize trial order where practical. Record success rate, completion latency in ms, timeout stage, per-rank skew, CUDA/NCCL errors, selected transport/interface, and cleanup outcome. Change one factor at a time in disposable runs: explicit interface, fresh rendezvous namespace, device mapping, or placement; never mask a failure by disabling safety checks. Compare observed traces against the hypothesis and reject it when the invariant passes but the failure persists, or when a competing factor changes outcome with other variables held constant.

Confounders and mitigations: scheduler placement, transient fabric faults, clock skew, warm caches, stale processes, retries, background load, version drift, and altered trial order can mimic causality; pin or record them, use fresh namespaces, synchronize clocks, and report failed/aborted trials separately. Set a bounded timeout, kill only owned child processes, verify no orphaned ranks, redact secrets and host-sensitive data, and obtain authorization before network or environment changes. Roll back temporary variables, interface overrides, debug settings, and files after each trial. Evidence is required before assigning a root cause; provisional conclusions should include confidence and the next discriminating measurement.
risks: rank/order diagnosis can be confounded by transient transport or scheduler faults
debug artifacts may expose topology or endpoint metadata
controlled trials can leave orphaned processes if watchdog cleanup fails
evidence_required: per-rank rendezvous and collective timestamps
fresh-namespace repeated all-reduce results across single-node, reduced-world, and full-world conditions
version, topology, interface, resource, and cleanup records
